title: Hull and tangent space of the deformation functor of a proper scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a proper $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $\mathrm{Art}_k$ have as objects commutative Artinian local $k$-algebras $R$ with identified residue field $k$, and as arrows local $k$-homomorphisms inducing the identity on $k$. Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize. Let $F_X(R)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of proper flat $R$-schemes $Y$ with an identification $Y\times_R k\cong X$, with isomorphisms preserving the identification [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product]. For a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra $B$ with residue field $k$, put $h_B(R)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k,\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{cont}}(B,R)$, using the maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. A transformation $h_B\to F_X$ is a hull when it has the lifting property for every surjection $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$ in $\mathrm{Art}_k$ and is a bijection at $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. There is such a hull. Its tangent space, and that of $F_X$, is canonically the finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(L_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$. Here $L_{X/k}$ is the cotangent complex in $D(\mathcal O_X)$: sheafify the normalized differential complex $\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/k}\otimes_{P_\bullet}\mathcal O_X$ of the standard simplicial polynomial resolution, in nonpositive degrees [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Ext means $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(-,-[j])$ in degree $j$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-ext]. The tangent identification commutes with restriction to open subschemes and with completion at closed points, interpreted using continuous differentials for completed rings. If every $k$-linear sheaf derivation $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$ is zero, the hull is a natural isomorphism $h_B\cong F_X$; thus $F_X$ is prorepresented by $B$.

source.place: Tags 0DY9 (lemma-schemes-TI), 0DYA (lemma-proper-schemes-TI) and 0ET5 (lemma-schemes-hull), equal-characteristic coefficient ring Lambda=k. The cotangent-complex formulation uses its truncation to the naive complex in degrees -1,0.

proof.text: For an Artinian local base $R$, its maximal ideal is nilpotent and $R$ is Noetherian. Hence properness reflection identifies the groupoid $\mathcal D_X(R)$ of all marked flat scheme deformations with that of proper flat ones: every such deformation has proper special fibre $X$. Base change preserves flatness and properness, so these groupoids and their isomorphism classes give the stated functor. Over $k$ a marked object has a unique marked isomorphism to $X$, so $\mathcal D_X(k)$ is equivalent to a point.

source.place: Tag 0ET5 (lemma-schemes-hull), comparison with Example 0DY7 (example-schemes); more-morphisms.tex Tag 09ZW.

proof.text: For $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ with $A_2\twoheadrightarrow A$, put $B=A_1\times_AA_2$. The infinitesimal affine-chart lemma identifies the base pushout with $\operatorname{Spec}B$. A pair of deformations with a specified identification over $A$ has a scheme pushout $Z$ over this base, recovering both deformations by that lemma. Each deformation is proper by step 1, and therefore locally finitely presented over its Noetherian Artinian base. Flat patching makes $Z$ flat and locally finitely presented; its canonical reconstruction map is invertible for every flat scheme. A pair of compatible morphisms glues uniquely by the universal property of the pushout. These identifications give inverse functors on objects and morphisms. The common marking over $k$ glues. Properness reflection makes $Z$ proper, since $B$ is again in $\mathrm{Art}_k$: Noetherianity and nilpotence make each $\mathfrak m_R^i/\mathfrak m_R^{i+1}$ finite-dimensional over $k$, so each input ring is finite-dimensional. The subring $B\subset A_1\oplus A_2$ is finite-dimensional, and its common residue map to $k$ has nilpotent kernel. Pairs of nonzero common residue are invertible componentwise, hence this kernel is its unique maximal ideal. Thus $\mathcal D_X$ has the full Rim-Schlessinger equivalence, including its specified gluing isomorphism.

Apply the square-zero lift torsor theorem to $\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. Its ideal is $k\epsilon$, and its pullback is $\mathcal O_X$ by $a\otimes c\epsilon\mapsto ca$. The trivial lift supplies the origin. This gives $T F_X\cong\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(L_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$, with the asserted $k$-linear structure. For the trivial lift an automorphism on its structure sheaf is $(a,b)\mapsto(a,b+D(a))$; multiplicativity is exactly $D(aa')=aD(a')+a'D(a)$ and the $k$-algebra condition is $D|_k=0$. Conversely each such derivation gives this automorphism, and composition adds derivations. Thus $\operatorname{Inf}(\mathcal D_X)=\operatorname{Der}_k(\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_X)$, without imposing any smoothness on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0DY9 (lemma-schemes-TI); defos.tex Tag 0D14, split origin and automorphism formula.

proof.text: Every affine chart of $X$ has a finitely generated $k$-algebra of sections, so it is Noetherian. The structure morphism is locally finitely presented because it is finite type over the Noetherian field. The cotangent truncation theorem gives $N=\tau_{\geq-1}L_{X/k}$ with coherent cohomology in degrees $-1,0$, coherent $\mathcal O_X$, and $\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(N,\mathcal O_X)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(L_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$. Apply proper coherent Ext finiteness over $k$ to $K=N$ and $E=\mathcal O_X[0]$. All its bounds hold, so this Ext group is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. This argument uses a coherent truncation and makes no assertion that the full cotangent complex is bounded below.

The groupoid in step 2 and the finite tangent space in steps 3–4 satisfy the abstract Schlessinger hull criterion with coefficient ring $k$. It supplies a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra $B$ and $h_B\to\pi_0\mathcal D_X=F_X$ with exactly the required surjective lifting map and tangent isomorphism. Composing its tangent isomorphism with step 3 gives the claimed canonical identification relative to the chosen hull. If all sheaf derivations vanish, the automorphism formula of step 3 makes the infinitesimal automorphism group trivial; the rigidity clause of the same criterion makes this hull itself an isomorphism on every Artinian base. This proves prorepresentation, without claiming that a hull is unique with a chosen ring identification.

Restriction to an open $U\subseteq X$ takes the same first-order structure-sheaf extension and trivial origin to their restrictions. The open-naturality clause of the lift torsor theorem therefore makes the tangent square with $\operatorname{Ext}^1(L,\mathcal O)$ commute. For a closed point $x$, choose an affine neighbourhood and localize its ring at $x$. The affine and localization clause of that theorem represents the restricted class by the conormal complex $C$ of a localized polynomial presentation. The completed-local comparison sends its class to $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}}(C\otimes\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x})$ and identifies it with the completed deformation. Its complex uses continuous differentials. Thus the completion square commutes, independently of the affine presentation, as claimed. The residue extension at $x$ need not be separable over $k$.
